subject.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted

question: After the PID-identity race is fixed, should OpenClaw intentionally override ACPX cooperative-cancel semantics by closing the live runtime and failing ACPX startup whenever process containment cannot be verified?
rationale: The stronger containment boundary is defensible, but it deliberately changes session reuse and startup availability beyond the upstream ACPX cancellation contract.

options.title: Fix identity race and adopt fail-closed
options.body: Revalidate ownership before escalation, then accept runtime reopen and startup refusal as the intended security contract.

options.title: Preserve cooperative cancel by default
options.body: Keep upstream-style session reuse and introduce strict containment only through a separately approved compatibility design.

options.title: Move the policy upstream
options.body: Pause this PR until the ACPX package owns and versions the containment and cancellation contract.

recommendation.title: Fix identity race and adopt fail-closed
recommendation.body: Revalidate ownership before escalation, then accept runtime reopen and startup refusal as the intended security contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cancellation and lease-cleanup contract originates in this contributor's merged ACP manager and ACPX work.
